How this is counted
  • A listen is a play that lasted at least 30 seconds. Shorter plays (skips) are not in the data at all.
  • 2017 is left out of every all-time number and ranking (totals, top artists / songs / albums, Versions, Rediscover). It still shows in per-year views: the 2017 chip, Years, Trending 2018 vs 2017, by-year charts and the monthly bars.
  • Live versions, remasters, radio and single edits, extended cuts, feat. and with tags, and Taylor's Versions count as the original song. The Versions tab breaks them out.
  • Remixes and acoustic versions stay separate songs. Podcasts and audiobooks are excluded.
  • Times are local: UTC-8 before August 1, 2021 and UTC-5 from then on, with no daylight saving. Years, months, days and hours all use this.
  • Everything is by calendar year. The export ends Nov 4, 2026, so 2026 is a partial year.
  • Hours are the time actually played. Album covers come from Spotify, artist photos from Deezer.

Versions: which take of a song you actually play

Everywhere else on the dashboard, every version of a song counts as that one song. A live take, an extended cut, a remaster, a radio edit, a "feat." version or a Taylor's Version all add up to the original. Albums work the same way: deluxe, expanded, anniversary and Taylor's Version editions count as one album (The Great Divide: The Last Of The Bugs is The Great Divide).

This page splits those listens back out so you can see which version you play most. Remixes and acoustic versions are different recordings, so they stay separate songs everywhere (compared at the bottom).

Lost favorites

Songs you fell for on their own and then lost: at least 20 all-time listens and not one in the last 18 months. The score is the listens in the song's busiest 90 days, times its share of everything you played by that artist (a song that carried the artist won't come back by playing the artist), times how long it's been quiet (full credit at 2 years). At most 2 songs per artist.
